original_question: Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ(σ, π) induced by those permutations τ in the interval [σ, π] with μ(σ, τ) not equal to 0. Determine whether Γ must always be pure, meaning that all of its maximal simplices have the same dimension.
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, open question (2) in the four-question list introduced by “In [19, Question 31] the following questions were raised”: “Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ induced by those elements τ of (σ, π) for which μ(σ, τ) ≠ 0. Is Γ a pure complex, that is, do all its maximal simplices (with respect to inclusion) have the same dimension?” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
correct_elements: Your draft has already identified the right open problem in §5.2, and it correctly focuses on the induced subcomplex Γ and on purity in the sense that all inclusion-maximal simplices have the same dimension. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
missing_details: The ambient object should be stated explicitly: P is the poset of all permutations ordered by classical pattern containment. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

Δ(σ, π) must be defined correctly: it is the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), obtained from [σ, π] by deleting σ and π. So the vertices relevant to Γ come from (σ, π), not from the whole closed interval [σ, π]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
A stand-alone formulation should say that μ is the Möbius function of the permutation pattern poset (or of its intervals). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether this purity statement holds for all permutations σ and π with σ < π. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses are relevant here; the omitted data are purely the poset/order-complex definitions and quantifiers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
refined_question: In the permutation pattern poset P ordered by classical pattern containment, for permutations σ < π let Δ(σ, π) denote the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), and let Γ be the induced subcomplex on those vertices τ ∈ (σ, π) for which the Möbius value μ(σ, τ) is nonzero. Must Γ always be a pure simplicial complex, i.e. must all of its inclusion-maximal simplices have the same dimension? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening because the survey states exactly this question in §5.2 and supplies the needed surrounding notation there: P is the permutation pattern poset, Δ(σ, π) is the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), and purity is explained immediately before the question list. Your draft is therefore close, but it is not fully stand-alone because it does not name the ambient poset and, more importantly, it blurs the paper’s distinction between the closed interval [σ, π] and the open interval (σ, π) whose order complex supplies the vertices of Γ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
